VOXEL-BASED MULTIPHYSICS SIMULATION

From geometry to physics. From simulation to design.

FOGUITOS is a voxel-based multiphysics simulation framework designed for power electronics and electronic hardware. It integrates geometry modeling, electrical analysis and thermal simulation within a modular computational framework, enabling engineers to investigate electrical losses, temperature distributions and electro-thermal interactions throughout the hardware design process.

From PCB traces and power semiconductor devices to magnetic components and complete power converters, FOGUITOS provides a unified approach to physics-based modeling and numerical simulation.

Simulation view

MODULAR SIMULATION WORKFLOW

One modular workflow, from geometry to temperature.

Import your design, define power losses and thermal boundary conditions, and obtain three-dimensional temperature distributions. Each module can be configured independently or combined into a complete electro-thermal simulation workflow.

  1. 01

    Geometry & Modeling

    Voxel model

    Import STL geometry exported from CAD and PCB Gerber files to construct three-dimensional voxel-based models. Assign material properties and configure individual components within a modular geometry representation.

    • CAD import (STL)
    • Gerber import
    • Voxelization
    • Material assignment
  2. 02

    Electrical Analysis & Power Losses

    Loss distribution

    Define component power dissipation directly or calculate DC resistive losses in PCB traces and winding conductors. Transfer the resulting spatial loss distribution to the thermal model.

    • User-defined power losses
    • PCB electrical analysis
    • Winding loss modeling
    • Joule heating
  3. 03

    Thermal Boundary Conditions

    Boundary conditions

    Configure convection coefficients, ambient or reference temperature, and surface boundary conditions. The thermal model accounts for solid conduction and prescribed convection.

    • Convection coefficients
    • Ambient temperature
    • Cooling conditions
    • Thermal radiation (future work)
  4. 04

    Thermal Simulation

    Temperature field

    Compute three-dimensional temperature fields under steady-state or time-dependent operating conditions. Visualize temperature evolution, local hotspots and the thermal response of individual components.

    • Steady-state analysis
    • Transient analysis
    • 3D temperature fields
    • Hotspot identification

Independent modules. Connected physics. One simulation framework.

UNIFIED MULTIPHYSICS FRAMEWORK

Multiple physics. One numerical framework.

Electrical and thermal problems are formulated through a common voxel-based representation and matrix-based numerical framework. Individual physics modules can operate independently or exchange physical quantities for coupled simulations.

  • DC Electrical Analysis

    Analyze the electrical behavior of conductive structures under DC operating conditions, including voltage distribution, current flow and resistive power losses.

    Voltage and current fields

    Key capabilities

    • Voltage drop
    • Current distribution
    • Electrical resistance
    • Joule losses

  • AC Electrical Analysis

    In development

    Research in frequency-dependent electrical modeling focuses on current redistribution and AC losses in conductive structures.

    AC current distribution

    Research directions

    • Frequency-dependent impedance
    • Skin effect
    • Proximity effect
    • AC conductor losses

  • Transient Thermal Analysis

    Compute the evolution of three-dimensional temperature fields for time-varying power dissipation and specified thermal boundary conditions.

    Transient temperature field

    Key capabilities

    • Time-dependent power profiles
    • Transient temperature fields
    • Explicit and implicit time integration
    • Thermal response and hotspot evolution

  • Steady-State Thermal Analysis

    Calculate equilibrium temperature distributions for specified power losses and thermal boundary conditions.

    Steady-state temperature field

    Key capabilities

    • Three-dimensional temperature distribution
    • Thermal equilibrium
    • Hotspot identification
    • Temperature gradients

THE NUMERICAL FOUNDATION

A common numerical foundation for different physics.

FOGUITOS represents physical domains through a common voxel-based discretization. Local physical interactions are assembled into matrix systems, providing a consistent numerical structure for electrical and thermal analysis.

This modular formulation allows individual solvers to share geometric representations, material information and physical quantities, supporting electro-thermal coupling and efficient numerical computation.

  2. Voxel-Based Discretization
  3. Matrix Assembly
  4. Electrical SolverThermal Solver
  5. Multiphysics Coupling

Transient system

Each physics module defines its own variables, coefficients and solution methods.

  • Shared Representation

    A common voxel-based representation for geometry, materials and physical interactions.

  • Modular Solvers

    Independent electrical and thermal solvers with consistent numerical interfaces.

  • Coupled Physics

    Electrical losses can be transferred to the thermal solver. Compatible DC workflows can recalculate those losses using temperature-dependent conductor resistivity.
